uncited: Sparse Voxel DAGs (SVDAGs) are a memory-efficient 3D data structure that extends the Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) by merging identical subtrees into shared nodes, forming a Directed Acyclic Graph [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].

While SVOs efficiently encode spatial sparsity, they store redundant copies of identical non-empty geometry, leading to high memory consumption at high resolutions [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].

SVDAGs solve this by allowing multiple parent nodes to share pointers to the same child instance, achieving lossless compression of topological redundancy without decompression overhead during traversal [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].

**Node Identity:** Two nodes are considered identical if they have the same `childmask` (encoding the existence of 8 children) and identical pointers to their respective children [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
**Bottom-Up Reduction:** The reduction process iterates from the leaves up to the root.
At each level, nodes are sorted by their identity key (childmask + child pointers) to group identical nodes together [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
**Compaction and Indirection:** Identical nodes are compacted into a single unique instance.
An indirection table maps original node positions to their unique counterparts, and parent pointers are updated to reference these unique instances [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
**Memory Layout:** Nodes store a `childmask` (8-bit integer) followed by an array of pointers to non-empty children [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
Node size varies between 8 and 36 bytes depending on the number of children (1 to 8) [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].

**Traversal:** Ray traversal leverages the DAG structure to traverse voxels in ray order, eliminating the need for contour intersection tests and distance maintenance required in standard SVOs [1147-sparse-voxel-dag-ray-traversal.md].

It addresses the memory bottleneck of SVOs at high resolutions (e.g., $128K^3$ grids) by exploiting the fact that complex 3D scenes often contain repeated geometric patterns [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
